source.title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities

accepted.question_text: Let B_d(G) = (R^d)^n be the configuration space of realizations P = (p_1, ..., p_n) of a graph G with n labeled vertices in R^d, and stratify B_d(G) by the equivalence classes of the self-stress spaces W(G, P) under sign-preserving homeomorphisms of fibers as in Definitions 1.2 and 1.3. Determine the combinatorial structure of the stratifications of B_2(K_6), B_3(K_4), and B_3(K_5), including the strata of all dimensions and the adjacency relations among those strata.
accepted.context_brief: Combinatorics of small tensegrity configuration spaces

evidence.quote: Problem 1 Describe the combinatorics of B2(K6), B3(K4) and B3(K5).

accepted.question_text: In the planar case d = 2, where strata are the maximal connected subsets of the configuration space whose self-stress fibers are sign-preservingly equivalent, classify all distinct types of strata that can occur for configurations of 10 labeled points.

evidence.quote: Let us say a few words about two-dimensional tensegrities.
The next case which contains unknown strata is n = 10 (see also Problem 8 below).
Problem 2 Describe all the possible different types of strata for 10 points.

accepted.question_text: In the planar tensegrity setting discussed immediately before Problem 3, compute, for each positive integer n, the number of different strata types that occur for configurations of n labeled points.
accepted.context_brief: Count planar strata types for n points

evidence.quote: Let us say a few words about two-dimensional tensegrities.
Problem 3 Compute the number of different types of strata for n points with arbitrary n.

accepted.question_text: Fix n and the paper's stratification of tensegrity configuration spaces by sign-preserving equivalence of self-stress fibers. Determine which subgraphs of the complete graph K_n induce the same stratification, i.e. partition the corresponding configuration space into the same strata.

evidence.quote: In many cases the strata for different graphs coincide. So it is natural to ask the following question.
Problem 4 Which subgraphs of Kn define the same stratifications?

accepted.question_text: Identify all strata of codimension greater than 1 in tensegrity configuration spaces that are not obtainable as intersections of closures of codimension-1 strata.

evidence.quote: Problem 5 Find all strata of codimension more than 1 that are not defined as an intersection of the closure of several codimension 1 strata.

accepted.question_text: In planar Cayley algebra, whose objects are points and lines in the plane and whose basic operations are join (forming the line through two points) and meet (forming the intersection point of two lines), determine when two Cayley algebra systems define the same tensegrity stratum.

evidence.quote: Majority of known examples in the planar case are expressed in terms of Cayley algebra.
Cayley algebra has two major operations:
Problem 6 Which Cayley algebra systems define the same strata?

accepted.question_text: For a given graph G in the plane, does there exist a Cayley algebra system, or finitely many such systems, whose solution set is exactly the union of the codimension-1 tensegrity strata in the planar configuration space B_2(G)?
accepted.context_brief: Cayley description of planar codimension-1 strata

evidence.quote: One of the main long-standing open problems on the Cayley strata description is as follows.

Problem 7 Given a graph G. Does there exist a Cayley algebra system (or several systems) describing the union of the codimension 1 tensegrity strata in the plane [i.e., the union of the codimension 1 strata of B2(Kn)]?

accepted.question_text: Develop a theory of geometric conditions that define strata for tensegrity configuration spaces in the multidimensional case, beyond the planar setting.

evidence.quote: There is almost nothing known in multidimensional case.
Problem 9 Develop theory of geometric conditions for strata in multidimensional case.
